scales.effort: 1 tiny, 2 small, 3 medium, 4 large, 5 very large. Derived from reference lines, then adjusted where the reference is bloated or unusually dense.
scales.risk: 1 routine, 2 some unknowns, 3 exactness or fidelity matters, 4 hard to verify or heavily unknown, 5 could invalidate the plan.
scales.difficulty: effort x risk. Bands: 1-4 green, 5-9 yellow, 10-14 orange, 15-25 red.
scales.progress: ported = the types exist and the project compiles. implemented = the module actually does what its spec says, and implementedNote says what was exercised to believe that. verified = checked against the oracle or a real corpus. Ported alone is scaffolding: 68 modules were once marked ported on 216 lines of skeleton, which is why the middle axis exists.

modules.name: Fixed-point math
modules.why: Determinism rests on it. A subtle rounding difference diverges every replay, and the symptom appears far from the cause.
modules.implementedNote: Golden vectors cover Q32.32 representation, arithmetic, square root, error cases, and vector magnitude/normalization invariants.

modules.name: Seeded RNG
modules.why: Must be reproducible across platforms and stable forever: changing the sequence invalidates every stored replay.
modules.implementedNote: SeededRandom implements deterministic PCG-XSH-RR, unbiased bounded uints, signed ranges, booleans, and Fix64 values; Atyria.Core.Tests passes with 31 tests including golden vectors and invalid-range cases.

modules.name: Ids, handles, pooling
modules.why: Shapes the allocation behaviour of everything above it, so getting it wrong is expensive to undo.
modules.implementedNote: EntityId, SlotId, pooled buffer lifecycle, primitive widths, equality, ordering, validation, and indexed access pass in Atyria.Core.Tests.

modules.name: Job system and frame pipeline
modules.why: The extract boundary between simulation and renderer is a data-layout decision, so it is taken now or not at all. Every other renderer feature can be added later; parallelism cannot.
modules.implementedNote: JobScheduler retains explicit Action draining and adds allocation-avoiding struct IJob dispatch through the thread pool; 32 core tests pass.

modules.name: Invariant guards
modules.why: Cheap, and it is what keeps the other invariants real. Each guard must be seen to fail.
modules.implementedNote: JobScheduler retains explicit Action draining and adds allocation-avoiding struct IJob dispatch through the thread pool; 32 core tests pass.

modules.name: Clean-room checking
modules.why: Protects the premise of the whole project, and a clean result proves less than people assume.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Oracle harness
modules.why: Every fidelity claim in phase 4 depends on it. Partly exists already as the playtest harness.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Frame benchmark and budget gate
modules.why: A deterministic scripted traversal reporting p50, p99 and per-pass milliseconds. Built before the renderer has features, because a budget nobody measures is a wish.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Archive container
modules.why: Format is trivial and already decoded once: 253 archives, 63,117 entries, zero failures.
modules.implementedNote: Reads the observed NeL BNP trailer index (directory offset in the final uint32, byte-sized names, uint32 size and position) through mapped spans; golden tests pass and the installed bagne_shapes.bnp corpus opens with 27 entries.

modules.name: Textures
modules.why: 27,370 files, 3.76 GB. Volume rather than subtlety, but a wrong decode is silent.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Meshes and CLOD
modules.why: 3,607 meshes with progressive level of detail. Bit-exact or nothing loads, and the failure surfaces in a log rather than on screen.
modules.implementedNote: ShapeStreamHeader decodes the observed SHAP/CMesh container prefix (signature, container version, type version) with a dirty-room golden vector in Atyria.Assets.Tests; MeshDefinition still uses a local synthetic contract for vertices/indices/LOD. Full .shape and MRM body decoding with two real LOD levels remains blocked on oracle corpus capture.

modules.name: Skeletons and animation
modules.why: 203 skeletons, 4,676 animations. Interpolation and track semantics have to match or everything moves wrongly.
modules.implementedNote: Skeleton bones preserve rest rotation; animation definitions, per-bone keyframe tracks, monotonic timestamp validation, endpoint sampling, fixed-point position interpolation, and normalized quaternion interpolation pass Atyria.Assets.Tests (43 tests).

modules.name: Terrain zones
modules.why: 7,561 zones, 1.49 GB, patch-based with tile banks. The densest format in the set.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Instance groups
modules.why: Already inspected: name, shape, transform, repeated. 5,148 files, about 51 instances per cell.
modules.implementedNote: Placed instances preserve shape/name, fixed-point position and scale, quaternion rotation, visibility, collision, and baked-lighting flags; parser tests pass in Atyria.Assets.Tests (43 tests).

modules.name: Collision data
modules.why: Feeds movement feel. A misread surface is felt rather than reported.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Sheet format
modules.why: 34 packed sheets carry items, bricks, phrases, creatures and the skill tree. One wrong offset corrupts the whole content set.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Primitives
modules.why: The populated world: spawns, NPCs, mission anchors. Licence of the data itself is unresolved.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Particle systems
modules.why: 870 systems. Large surface, but a wrong one is visible immediately rather than silently.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Graphics backend
modules.why: C# hands you no GPU abstraction, so this is written here: Vulkan 1.3, one backend for Windows and Linux, bindless and GPU-driven. The open measurement is the cost of recording commands from managed code, and it is the one that could still invalidate the plan.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Frame graph
modules.why: Passes declare what they read and write; barriers and transient memory are derived once and cached. Hand-written Vulkan barriers across a dozen passes is where the bugs live.
modules.implementedNote: Bounded allocation-free pass graph validates capacity, duplicate/unknown dependencies, stable topological order, and bounds; FrameGraphTests cover the contract vectors.

modules.name: Terrain rendering
modules.why: Whether this holds the reference's draw distance inside the 1.8 ms terrain budget is UNMEASURED. First risk to retire.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Mesh and skinning
modules.why: Well-understood problem, large surface. Instancing decides whether crowds are affordable.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Lighting, shadows and global illumination
modules.why: Not a port. Cascaded shadows, deferred lighting and re-baked GI are what make 2004 geometry read as lit. Budgeted at 2.0 ms of the 7.1 ms GPU frame.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Particle rendering
modules.why: Visual, self-evident when wrong. GPU-simulated, lit and depth-faded, with density a player setting: the same art, orders of magnitude more of it.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Sky, atmosphere, weather and time of day
modules.why: The highest visual return in the project, and it costs no art: a landscape reads almost entirely through its air. A 2004 skybox with a fog colour is why 2004 landscapes look 2004.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Vegetation
modules.why: Density is a frame-time problem as much as a visual one, and a modern GPU affords 10 to 50 times the 2004 count of the same art.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Post-processing and tonemapping
modules.why: Not a port. Real tonemapping, GTAO, bloom, reflections and grading cost no art at all and change every frame in the game. Each one individually switchable.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Anti-aliasing and upscaling
modules.why: TAA with FSR as the vendor-neutral baseline, DLSS and XeSS optional. The main lever for reaching 140 fps on weak hardware, which makes it a performance module as much as an image one.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Deterministic capture
modules.why: Golden-frame testing depends on it being genuinely deterministic, not approximately.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Cell grid and residency
modules.why: Naming and neighbourhood are simple; getting eviction wrong shows up as thrash.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Streaming and budget
modules.why: Where the GC argument is won or lost. Must not allocate in the hot path, and 6.4 GB must stay off the managed heap.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Collision and movement surface
modules.why: This IS game feel. Sliding along a wall and stepping over a lip decide whether movement feels right, and approximation is noticed immediately.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Spatial index
modules.why: Shared by client and server. If the two disagree, players fall through the world.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Wire schema compiler
modules.why: 474 properties and 335 impulses. A previous attempt assumed flat message ids and was wrong: addressing is a route through the tree.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Bit-packed codec
modules.why: Bit widths come from sibling counts, so adding an entry re-encodes a branch. Silent corruption if wrong.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Transport and sessions
modules.why: Transport choice is still open. QUIC would also open a browser path later.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Property replication
modules.why: Interest scoping and per-client bandwidth priority decide whether a crowded scene feels right.
modules.implementedNote: Replication vectors cover bounded storage, same-value suppression, dirty update collection, slot ordering, and overflow retention.

modules.name: Authoritative tick
modules.why: Gameplay timing is expressed in ticks, so extraction converts every duration to wall-clock time once. After that the rate is free: it starts at the reference's 10 Hz and can rise for responsiveness without rescaling a single cooldown.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Session and admission
modules.why: Well-understood territory, and the one place the existing web-API patterns apply in full.
modules.implementedNote: Structural vectors cover initial state, admission, duplicate/full rejection, lookup, release, count tracking, zeroed failure outputs, and session-number reuse in Atyria.Server.Tests.

modules.name: Entity registry
modules.why: Lifecycle and visibility. Allocation behaviour here is felt at every tick.
modules.implementedNote: EntityRegistry covers unique valid IDs, O(1) dictionary lookup, removal deactivation, clear, count, and invalid/duplicate registration vectors in Atyria.Server.Tests.

modules.name: Movement and modes
modules.why: Game feel, and the first thing a player judges. Fixed-point and collision have to agree exactly.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Combat resolution
modules.why: The most fidelity-critical code in the project. Hit tables and effect ordering cannot be re-derived by reasoning, only matched against the oracle. Note: sabrina is the DEAD copy.
modules.implementedNote: CombatResolver retains the scalar health contract and now exposes typed ten-channel protection with cap-before-reduction ordering; CombatTables expose observed quality 1-21 weapon, armor, and bounded hit-chance tables as integer fixed-point data, while full hit/effect integration and oracle verification remain pending.

modules.name: Persistent effects
modules.why: One file per effect in the reference. Stacking and ordering are behaviour.
modules.implementedNote: Bounded effect replacement/stack identity, explicit pair removal, tick-based expiry, slot-order span collection, capacity, and invalid-input behavior pass in Atyria.Sim.Tests.

modules.name: Magic resolution
modules.why: Cast, resist, apply. Same exactness bar as combat.
modules.implementedNote: Fixed-point magic cast, direct-resistance table lookup/interpolation, channel-specific persistent modifiers, explicit clear, and damage-factor resolution cover successful casts, clipped levels, partial success, resistance rejection/cap, factor validation, mana exhaustion, invalid cost/power, state preservation, zero-cost casts, and result reporting; full spell-family integration remains oracle-pending.

modules.name: Craft and harvest
modules.why: Foraging is a signature system and its success curves are tuned, not derivable.
modules.implementedNote: CraftResolver validates positive integer inputs and available materials, consumes only on success, and passes the documented structural vectors; oracle comparison remains pending.

modules.name: Character, stats, progression
modules.why: character.cpp alone is 21,550 lines and character.h is included by 188 files. Large, coupled, and full of tuned numbers.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Inventory and equipment
modules.why: Weight, bulk and slot rules are mechanical but numerous.
modules.implementedNote: Structural vectors cover stack merging, slot-order removal, capacity and invalid-input rejection, and query consistency in Atyria.Sim.Tests.

modules.name: Mob behaviour
modules.why: Aggro, groups and spawn cycles. Most behaviour is group-level, not per-creature, and it is judged by feel over time.
modules.implementedNote: AiController perception radius, chase/attack/disengage state machine and deterministic fauna spawning/grazing/resting cycle with one-bot-per-update population ramp; AiBehaviorTests pass. Aggro groups and full place selection remain pending.

modules.name: Missions
modules.why: Large but mostly declarative once primitives are extracted.
modules.implementedNote: MissionInstance tracks multi-objective progress and completion; MissionManagerTests pass in Atyria.Sim.Tests.

modules.name: Guilds and factions
modules.why: Social systems: broad, shallow, low exactness bar.
modules.implementedNote: Guild roster add/remove with rank and leader protection; GuildDefinitionTests pass in Atyria.Sim.Tests.

modules.name: Outposts
modules.why: Self-contained gameplay with its own timing rules.
modules.implementedNote: Structural vectors cover neutral initialization, partial contest, threshold transfer, progress reset, and controller recovery in Atyria.Sim.Tests.

modules.name: Trade and economy
modules.why: Exploitable if wrong, so it needs care disproportionate to its size.
modules.implementedNote: Structural vectors cover listing validation, cancellation, purchase overflow, trade confirmation, atomic settlement, rollback constraints, and cancellation state in Atyria.Sim.Tests.

modules.name: Chat and server text
modules.why: Routing plus localisation of server-sent player text.
modules.implementedNote: Structural vectors cover private delivery, broadcast delivery, missing recipients, null messages, invalid channels, replacement subscriptions, and unsubscribe behavior in Atyria.Server.Tests.

modules.name: Persistence
modules.why: The reference has a bespoke engine; a database replaces it. Migration correctness matters more than speed.
modules.implementedNote: InMemoryPersistenceStore saves and loads PlayerDataRecord async; PersistenceStoreTests pass in Atyria.Server.Tests.

modules.name: Widget engine
modules.why: Layout, event routing, text and bindings. Large, but a well-understood problem.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Property bindings
modules.why: The link between the property tree and the HUD. If a value is missing, the work is a contract change.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: HUD definitions
reference: interfaces_v3 (53,150 lines of markup and script)
modules.why: RE-AUTHORED window by window from observation, never converted: transforming their markup carries its expression. Paid across features rather than upfront.
modules.implementedNote: hud/windows/ JSON definitions load via HudWindowLoader; UIWindow supports pointer dragging and deterministic docking, while WindowManager handles z-order/focus; 7 UI tests pass.

modules.name: Action handlers
modules.why: The verbs the HUD invokes. Numerous and individually simple.
modules.implementedNote: UIActionRouter registers and dispatches named handlers with optional parameters; Atyria.Ui.Tests passes structural vectors.

modules.name: Client core and session
modules.why: Boot, session, entity view, camera, prediction. Broad rather than deep.
modules.implementedNote: ClientSession lifecycle, ClientMirror property deltas, and ClientHost UDP hello/tick/delta loop compile and pass structural tests in Atyria.Client.Tests; oracle comparison remains pending.

modules.name: Visual entities and animation state
modules.why: Appearance composition and animation blending. Visible immediately when wrong.
modules.implementedNote: Client entity vectors cover transform interpolation, EAnimationState target blending, manager tick batching, visible entity add/remove, and invalid ID rejection; ClientEntityTests pass.

modules.name: Graphics settings and presets
modules.why: Every option is data carrying its measured cost in milliseconds. Presets are derived from measurement rather than taste, and first run auto-detects by benchmarking instead of matching GPU name strings.
modules.implementedNote: Settings vectors cover defaults/reset, JSON persistence, missing or malformed file fallback, and resolution/volume normalization; 10 client tests pass.

modules.name: Sound
modules.why: Mature libraries exist; only the bank and sound-animation formats need decoding.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Content extraction
modules.why: Fails quietly: a run that drops a category looks exactly like one that worked. Counts must reconcile on both sides.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Material uplift and GI bake
modules.why: Offline. Derives normal and roughness from diffuse-only 2004 textures, delights the albedo, and re-bakes global illumination from the existing geometry. Compute time instead of artist time; derived maps inherit the art licence.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Rebrand mapping
modules.why: The brand seam. An unmapped term must fail extraction rather than travel downstream into a shipped build.
modules.implementedNote: Implementation and structural tests were present in the verified worktree snapshot at resume.

modules.name: Control plane
modules.why: Time control, state queries, snapshots, injection. Must be compiled out of release builds, not merely disabled.
modules.implementedNote: QaController steps GameClock, spawns entities, and snapshots EntityRegistry state; Atyria.Qa.Tests passes structural vectors.

modules.name: Scenario runner
modules.why: Turns a seed plus an input sequence into a complete, replayable bug report.
modules.implementedNote: ScenarioRunner executes registered IGameScenario instances against QaController; Atyria.Qa.Tests passes structural vectors.

modules.name: MCP bridge
modules.why: The thin part. A transport over capability that already exists.
modules.implementedNote: tools/mcp/bridge.mjs exposes step_ticks, get_clock_info, and get_active_entities over JSON-RPC stdin/stdout per qa.mcp spec.
